payload.name: Extract Explicit Plans and Intentions
payload.description: Use when a speaker states what they plan to do, intend, or want to do regarding an event, project, or upcoming occasion.
content: During extraction, treat explicit first-person statements of intention (e.g., 'I want to...', 'I plan to...', 'I'm going to...') as memory-worthy and create a plan memory for the speaker when the statement expresses what they intend to do.

If a plan is tied to an already-extracted event or project candidate, either include the stated plan in that event memory or create a separate plan candidate; do not drop the plan while summarizing the event.
Stop after capturing the stated plan and its target event; do not infer additional plans or expand the scope.

candidates.solves: When a speaker explicitly states a plan or intention for an upcoming event or project, extraction sometimes records only the event overview and omits the stated plan, making it impossible to answer future questions about what the speaker intends to do. This Skill ensures explicit first-person plans are captured as plan memories or included in the related event memory.

payload.name: Extract Job Start Events from Casual Mentions
payload.description: When a speaker mentions starting a new job, position, or role, even in small talk, during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement that the speaker started a new job, position, or role as an event candidate, even if it appears in casual conversation or as an aside.
Include the job title or role and any stated start time; resolve relative time like 'last week' against the message timestamp to compute the actual date.
Record the speaker as the subject and use memory kind 'event'; do not fold the job start into a pet, project, or preference candidate.
Stop after capturing the stated job change; do not infer employer, salary, or other details unless explicitly mentioned.

candidates.solves: Construction pipelines often ignore explicit life changes such as starting a new job when they appear in casual small talk, so later questions about when the person began the role cannot be answered. This skill ensures job/role start statements are extracted as dated event memories.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Collaboration Agreements
payload.description: When two participants explicitly agree or decide to collaborate on a shared activity or content, extract it as a memory candidate, even if the agreement is stated enthusiastically or in casual wording.
content: During extraction, treat an explicit mutual agreement to collaborate on a shared activity (e.g., creating content, working on a project, managing accounts) as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the collaborators, the agreed activity, and the date/time of the agreement from the message or session timestamp.
When the agreement is confirmed in a later message after earlier offers or interest, the final confirming message is sufficient evidence; create one candidate for the decision.
Stop after capturing the agreement; do not infer outcomes, add unspoken tasks, or create separate memories for every enthusiastic reply.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes fail to persist explicit agreements to collaborate when they are expressed in casual or enthusiastic language at the end of a multi-turn discussion, even though earlier offers and advice were captured. This Skill ensures mutual collaboration decisions are extracted as event or relationship memories with the parties, the agreed activity, and the timestamp.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Motivational Drivers
payload.description: Use when a speaker explicitly states what motivates or drives them or their group to improve, persist, or succeed.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly names what motivates or drives them or their group to improve, persist, or succeed, create a state or preference candidate capturing the driver and the subject, even if the message is small talk or contains no direct question.
Do not require the motivation to be tied to a named project; capture the stated reason from everyday narrative and resolve relative time from the session timestamp.
Stop after capturing the explicitly stated driver; do not infer additional unstated motivations or add unrelated details.

candidates.solves: Extraction misses explicit statements that name what motivates or drives a speaker or their group to improve, persist, or succeed, because these statements are often brief, occur in casual conversation, and are not tied to a named project or question.

payload.name: Extract Discovered Places as Event Memories
payload.description: When a speaker reports finding, discovering, checking out, or stumbling upon a place (park, open space, cafe, spot), during extraction or when updating a plan memory.
content: During extraction, when a message states that the speaker or the speaker and others found, discovered, checked out, or stumbled upon a place, create a separate event memory capturing who, what place, and when; do not store it only as a plan or intention.
If a later message reports visiting that discovered place, update or keep that event memory instead of folding the visit into a plan memory.
During CRUD, when updating a plan memory, preserve any earlier discovered/visited place facts as distinct event memories; do not overwrite them with new plans or object_text changes.
Stop after capturing the discovered place once; do not add duplicate memories for later casual mentions.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes record only a future plan (e.g., intending to hike) and fail to store an already-completed discovery or visit of a place, so later updates to the plan lose the fact that the place was checked out. This skill ensures discovered/visited places are stored as separate event memories and preserved during plan updates.

payload.name: Preserve All Stated Intentions in Event Plans
payload.description: When extracting an event or plan where the speaker explicitly states multiple intentions or reasons, include every stated reason in the memory candidate.
content: During extraction, if a message states why the speaker plans to attend or do something, capture every explicitly stated intention or reason in the event/plan candidate.
Scan the source message for all purpose clauses (e.g., 'to ...', 'because ...', 'so that ...') and list each one; do not paraphrase away or merge distinct reasons.
Stop after all stated reasons are included; do not add unmentioned motives.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes paraphrase a memory candidate and drop one of several explicitly stated reasons or intentions behind a plan or event, causing later questions about the person's motivation to fail. This skill ensures every explicitly stated purpose is preserved in the extracted event or plan memory.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Stated Preferences
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states what they enjoy, like, or prefer (e.g., types of films, books, activities), even in a turn that also mentions a project or plan.
content: During extraction, create a preference memory whenever a speaker explicitly states something they enjoy or like, even if the same turn includes a project, plan, or other event.
Do not let a project-focused extraction replace or suppress the explicit preference; each explicitly stated preference should be its own candidate.
Extract only the categories or items explicitly named as enjoyed, and stop after capturing the stated likes; do not infer additional genres or preferences.

candidates.solves: Conversations often mix several facts in one turn. When a user explicitly states a preference (such as enjoying a type of film) alongside a project, plan, or other event, the construction agent may capture only the project and drop the preference, causing a missing memory for later questions. This skill ensures explicit preference statements are extracted independently.

payload.name: Extract Brief Planned Gatherings and Events
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly mentions organizing, hosting, or planning an event or gathering, even briefly in small talk, during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly says they are organizing, hosting, or planning an event or gathering (e.g., party, meetup, tournament, get-together), create an event candidate capturing the event, the organizer, and any explicit time reference, even when the mention is brief or embedded in a reply about someone else's plans.

Resolve relative time references (e.g., 'this weekend', 'two weekends later') using the message/session timestamp to an absolute date or at least the month, so future temporal questions can be answered.
Create one candidate per announced event and stop once the organizer, event, and time are captured; do not infer guests, location, or other details that are not explicitly stated.

candidates.solves: Construction misses explicit planned events or gatherings announced in small talk, especially when the speaker is replying to another person's plans. The system should extract the event, organizer, and a resolved time reference even from a brief sentence so future questions about what someone is organizing can be answered.

payload.name: Extract New Activity Intentions and Tryouts
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker expresses interest in, plans to try, or states they are trying a new hobby or activity, including in reply to a suggestion.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly says they are considering, planning, or starting a new hobby or activity, create a candidate memory for that activity with any stated timeframe.
Use memory kind 'event' when the speaker states they will try or are trying it; otherwise use 'preference' or 'state' for interest alone.
Do not skip such statements because they are replies, small talk, or acknowledgments; treat the speaker's own stated intention as sufficient evidence.
Capture only the activity and facts explicitly stated; do not infer acceptance of an unmentioned suggestion, and stop once the activity is captured.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, MERGE or UPDATE it instead of creating a duplicate.

candidates.solves: The construction agent sometimes fails to extract a speaker's own adoption of a new hobby or activity when it appears in casual replies to suggestions, treating the message as small talk or as belonging only to the other speaker's offer. This skill ensures explicit intentions to try or take up an activity become durable memories.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Business or Venture Status
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states the current condition of their business, store, or venture, extract it as a state memory.
content: During extraction, when a speaker reports the current status of a business, store, or venture they own or run (e.g., 'doing great', 'struggling'), create a state memory with subject=speaker, the named entity, and the stated status.
Set world_start to the message/session date and use only explicit wording; do not infer status from enthusiasm, obstacles, or future plans.
Stop after capturing the stated status; do not add unrelated details from the same message unless they are separate explicit facts.

candidates.solves: During memory extraction, explicit statements about the current condition of a person's business, store, or venture are often skipped because existing skills focus on projects, events, and emotional support. This Skill ensures these direct status assertions are captured as durable state memories so future questions about the business can be answered.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Motivations for Ongoing Improvement
payload.description: When a user explicitly states what motivates or inspires them to keep improving at an activity, even as a reflective aside without a question, project, or event.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly states a love, passion, or reason that motivates them to keep improving at an activity, create a preference or state memory capturing both the activity and the stated motivator; do not skip the turn because the statement is reflective, contains no question, or is not attached to a project or event.
Keep the stated motivator as its own facet in the memory rather than merging it into a vague preference summary or inferring additional unstated reasons.
Stop after capturing the explicitly stated motivator and its immediate activity; do not broaden to other activities or projects from the same session.

candidates.solves: Construction agents often omit explicit motivational statements when they appear in reflective conversation rather than as a project, goal, or event. This Skill ensures that a user's stated love, passion, or reason for improving is captured as a preference or state memory.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Events on Update
payload.description: When a new message describes an event or fact that differs from an existing memory (different date, milestone, or topic), before applying an UPDATE verify whether the existing memory is truly the same fact; otherwise ADD a separate memory.
content: During the CRUD/update stage, before applying UPDATE to an existing memory, check whether the new message describes the same event/fact as the existing memory (same subject, same event type, and same time period).
If the new message describes a distinct event, even with the same people, do not overwrite the existing memory; create a new ADD candidate for the new event.
Preserve the original memory's content, world_start, and facts unless the new message explicitly corrects or supersedes that same fact.

When two related but different events exist (e.g., a pregnancy announcement and a later marriage announcement), keep them as separate memories and only update one when the new evidence directly revises that same memory.

candidates.solves: Prevents a later message about a different event from overwriting an earlier distinct memory during construction updates. When a new message involves the same people but describes a separate milestone, date, or topic, the agent should ADD a new memory instead of UPDATE-ing the old one, preserving previously stored facts.

payload.name: Preserve Prior Facts on Memory Update
payload.description: When updating an existing memory about a project or activity, if the new message adds details or mentions a related topic without explicitly contradicting the stored facts, preserve the original facts instead of overwriting them.
content: During UPDATE on an existing memory, first compare the new message's claims with the memory's current explicit facts.

If the new message only adds detail, reframes the topic, or mentions a related project, do not replace the existing memory; instead add a new candidate or merge only the genuinely new attributes while keeping the original facts unchanged.

Only overwrite a stored fact when the new message explicitly contradicts it. When it does, preserve the old factual span by setting world_end or retaining the older version, and do not move world_start unless the message explicitly corrects the start date.
Stop after deciding the update; do not search for additional evidence or expand the memory beyond what the message states.

candidates.solves: The Construction Agent sometimes replaces a previously stored, still-valid fact (e.g., a project name or start date) when a later message describes a related but different aspect of the same activity. This destroys evidence needed for temporal queries. This skill prevents destructive overwrites by requiring an explicit contradiction before replacing facts, and by keeping old facts or creating separate memories when the new message merely adds or shifts topic.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Event Memories on Update
payload.description: When a later message describes a different event than an existing memory, during CRUD, do not overwrite the existing event; add a separate memory and preserve prior facts.
content: During CRUD, before UPDATEing an event memory, check whether the incoming fact is the same event (same activity and time) as the stored memory. If it is a different event, do not overwrite; ADD a new event memory.
When the incoming message enriches the same event, UPDATE or MERGE may be used, but preserve any previously stored distinct facts that remain true.
Never reuse a memory ID for an unrelated event just because the subject, companion, or memory kind matches; each distinct activity/event needs its own memory.
Stop once the new event is stored; do not add duplicate memories for repeated mentions of the same event.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of previously stored event facts when a later message describes a different activity for the same person or companion. The agent may incorrectly UPDATE an existing event memory in place, replacing its activity and date with the new event instead of creating a separate memory.

payload.name: Verify Redundancy Before Skipping Candidate
payload.description: Use during CRUD/decision when a candidate is about to be SKIPped as already covered or updated; verify the referenced memory actually exists before skipping.
content: During CRUD/decision stage, before marking any candidate as SKIP for redundancy, verify that a memory containing the same facts actually exists in the retrieved existing-memory pool or was accepted earlier in the current batch.
If the skip reason references an 'updated memory' that cannot be found in the pool or in accepted updates, do not skip; instead ADD or UPDATE to persist the candidate.
Only skip when the identical information is verifiably present in the relevant memory records; when in doubt, keep the candidate to avoid information loss.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of extracted facts when the Construction Agent skips a candidate believing the information already exists in an updated memory, but no such memory is actually present in the current pool or batch. Instills a verification step before SKIP decisions to ensure redundancy claims are grounded in real memory records.

payload.name: Preserve Existing Facts in Memory Merge
payload.description: During CRUD, when merging or updating an existing memory with new evidence, use this guidance to prevent older facts from being overwritten.
content: During CRUD, before applying a MERGE or UPDATE to an existing memory, read the current version's content and list every concrete fact it stores (activities, preferences, events, relationships).
Apply the change as a superset: keep all those existing facts in the new version, adding or replacing only content the new evidence explicitly changes or contradicts.
If the new evidence concerns a different topic with no explicit contradiction, create a separate memory for it and leave the existing memory unchanged instead of merging unrelated content.
After writing the new version, verify that every previously stored concrete fact is still present; restore any that were dropped.
Stop once old facts are preserved and new evidence is incorporated; do not add unrelated inferences or extra memories.

candidates.solves: Memory construction loses previously stored facts when a later MERGE or UPDATE replaces an existing memory's content with new evidence instead of combining them. This skill ensures CRUD operations preserve the old memory's concrete facts while adding new evidence, and avoid merging unrelated topics into one memory.

payload.name: Keep Specific Events Not Covered by General Memories
payload.description: When deciding whether to ADD or SKIP an event candidate and the only existing memory is a broader general statement, ADD the event instead of skipping it as already represented.
content: During CRUD decisions, compare an event candidate against existing memories for the same concrete occurrence: same subject, action, object, time, and emotional reaction.

If the existing memory states only a general trait, preference, or impact and does not already contain the specific event details, do not SKIP as already represented; ADD or MERGE the event candidate.
Preserve the distinct event even when it illustrates a broader theme, because later questions may ask about the specific episode or feeling.
Stop after one event per occurrence; do not add multiple paraphrases of the same event.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of specific episodic facts during memory construction when a candidate is incorrectly skipped because a general memory about the same person or topic already exists. It preserves concrete events and feelings that may be asked about later.

payload.name: Verify Existing Memory Before SKIP
payload.description: When a construction CRUD decision is about to SKIP a candidate because it claims the information is already covered by an existing memory, use this skill.
content: During CRUD, before SKIPping a candidate as duplicate or already covered, confirm the covering memory is present in the current retrieved memory pool and explicitly contains the same fact.
If no matching memory exists, ADD the candidate; do not infer coverage from earlier sessions or from a general sense that the topic was discussed.
Only UPDATE or MERGE when the existing memory is verified; if the pool lacks the memory, adding preserves the new evidence.

candidates.solves: Prevents construction decisions from skipping newly extracted evidence by assuming it is already stored. A candidate is dropped as a duplicate even though no matching memory exists in the retrieved pool, so the fact is never persisted and later questions cannot be answered.

payload.name: Merge New Category Members into Existing Memory Instead of Replacing
payload.description: When a user reveals an additional item in a category already stored or likely to be stored (e.g., allergies, dietary restrictions, dislikes), during extraction or update.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly states a restriction or attribute in a recurring category (e.g., allergies, dietary limits, dislikes), create a candidate for that fact even when it appears in casual conversation; do not wait for a direct question.

During CRUD, when a new candidate adds another member of a category already present in an existing memory (e.g., another allergy on a memory that lists allergies), do not replace the existing content with only the new member. Preserve previously stored members and append the new one in the same memory or merge into it.

Use a correction/overwrite only when the new statement explicitly contradicts or supersedes an earlier fact; for additive facts, keep prior content and record the new item with its own evidence and date.
After merging, stop; do not expand into exhaustive searches or add unrelated memories.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of previously stored facts when a later message adds another member of the same category (e.g., an additional allergy or dietary restriction). The agent replaced the whole memory with only the new item and also skipped extracting the first mention of a related restriction, so later answers missed earlier facts.

payload.name: Preserve prior specifics when enriching memories
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory, use this if the new content is more general, emotional, or abstract than the stored fact, or if the update would drop previously captured details.
content: During CRUD, before updating or merging an existing memory, compare the new content against the stored facts. Preserve every specific, time-bound fact already captured (e.g., doctor visits, diagnoses, dates, locations) unless directly contradicted by new evidence.

If new messages add broader context such as general struggles, feelings, or quotes about the same topic, do not replace the concrete earlier fact with that framing. Create an enriched version that keeps the old specifics and appends the new nuance.

If an update would remove a previously captured fact that is not contradicted, treat the update as a loss: retain the old detail and add the new information instead. Stop once the memory contains both the preserved facts and the relevant new context; do not expand into unrelated details.

candidates.solves: During CRUD, an existing memory that contains a concrete, time-bound fact is sometimes overwritten by a later, more general summary that drops the fact, making it impossible to answer future questions about the specific event. This Skill ensures updates preserve previously stored specifics while incorporating new context.
